title: Qualitative integral localization from ordinary recollement and finite records
statement: Fix a field k, a prime l invertible in k, a finite extension E/Q_l, a separated finite-type k-scheme X with structure morphism t, and complementary closed/open immersions i:Z→X and j:U→X. Given a family F n : SfFiniteLocalization l E n k i j [def-sf-localization-stage-data] and ordinary recollement O : SfIntegralOrdinaryRecollement l E i j [lem-sf-integral-ordinary-recollement-realization], the qualitative comparison record SfIntegralLocalizationComparisonData l E k hl t i j F [def-sf-integral-localization-comparison-data] is nonempty. This conclusion contains no finite-stage existence assertion no integral image limit existence, and no integral quantitative Tor field; all five integral reduction comparisons include the same prescribed adjunction equations.

source.place: Integral stage: actual completed images, supported triangle, normalized exceptional and open reduction comparisons.

proof.text: Use the supplied O: restrict the actual ambient kernel right adjoint and use its restricted exceptional adjunction, ordinary closed/open adjunctions, and completed image and pullback comparisons. Transport the ordinary supported triangle through the invertible ordinary-to-completed pullback comparison. The normalized adjunction equations identify its maps with the restricted counit and open unit. Shifted Hom orthogonality makes the boundary unique and natural. Full faithfulness of closed image gives the exceptional unit; its Hom adjunction and orthogonality give exceptional-open vanishing. Fullness identifies the restricted pullbacks with constructibleIntegralPullback.

O gives actual direct-image reduction. Its pull_reduction, computed on a K-flat representative, and the normalized completed pullback reduction of [lemma-weil-pbc-completed-pullback-reduction] give both pullback reductions. Lift these natural isomorphisms along the full intrinsic constructible inclusions. Each finite record in F has its image and pullbacks compared to these same ambient operations; conjugate the reduction isomorphisms by those comparisons.

Build the ordinary/finite kernel presentation from O and the finite adjunctions and triangles. Restrict the canonical counit transpose alphaOf to constructible inputs. [lem-sf-exceptional-reduction-transition-comparison] makes it invertible and proves its exceptional-counit and open-unit equations. The unique adjoint isomorphism preserving the counit compares the finite kernel presentation with the exceptional adjunction of F n. Conjugate the equations with this same comparison and the ordinary-operation comparisons to obtain exactly the two recorded equations. Assemble the qualitative comparison data; no finite cohomological dimension or Tor assumption is used.
